title: On Borrowing two books from the school
subtitle: 学校教育 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）
meta: 主题语境：学校教育（人与自我·生活与学习·学校生活与学习）　|　核心词汇：borrow　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 borrow 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 the musician ① borrowed two books from the school in public, and every listener in the hall said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the musician ② borrows two books from the school in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ borrow two books from the school at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ borrowed two books from the school before — a line in the programme for December 1955 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Borrowing two books from the school in public, the musician said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the score at the far piano, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ borrow their way of saying it in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Borrow their way of saying it at once and never mention it again.

By 1968 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new listener from the next hall ⑧ borrows their way of saying it in public every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the piano, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ borrowed two books from the school again when nobody else would.

⑩ To borrow two books from the school, my mother said in 1973, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the hall remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the hall forgets, somebody borrows two books from the school in silence again and somebody must borrow two books from the school in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 借入（一般过去式 borrowed two books from the school：1961 年乐师头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 借入（一般现在 borrows two books from the school：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 借入（不定式 to borrow two books from the school：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 借入（过去完成时 had borrowed two books from the school：1955 年十二月的节目单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 借入（动名词 borrowing two books from the school 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 借用（borrow their way of saying it：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去借用他们那种说法）
G. v. 借用（borrow their way of saying it：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 借入（后段两处：新来的听客照例 borrows their way of saying it，而母亲又一次 borrowed two books from the school）

answers.why: borrow 意为“借入”，1961 年乐师当着众人面借入从学堂借来两本书，那是音乐厅里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 borrowed。
borrow 意为“借入”，自那以后乐师一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 borrows。
borrow 意为“借入”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯借入从学堂借来两本书”，此处为不定式 to borrow two books from the school。
borrow 意为“借入”，节目单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1968 年之前就有人借入过，故用过去完成时 had borrowed。
borrow 意为“借入”，乐师说“借入从学堂借来两本书这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 borrowing two books from the school 作主语。
borrow 意为“借用”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去借用他们那种说法”，should ever 之后用原形 borrow their way of saying it。
borrow 意为“借用”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻借用他们那种说法（borrow their way of saying it at once），以后再也不要提起。
borrow 意为“借入”，新来的听客每个夜晚都照例借用他们那种说法，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 borrows。
borrow 意为“借入”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面借入从学堂借来两本书，用一般过去式 borrowed 叙述。
borrow 意为“借入”，结尾那句是母亲 1973 年的话：要借入从学堂借来两本书，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和音乐厅记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 borrow 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1961 the musician borrowed two books from the school in public, and nobody in the hall forgot it.
Even now the musician borrows two books from the school in silence whenever the hall asks.
Borrowing two books from the school in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever borrow their way of saying it in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new listener from the next hall borrows their way of saying it in public every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother borrowed two books from the school again, and the hall remembered that half.
